title: Repair a Key-value Parser
summary: Fix parsing that uses the wrong delimiter.

contract.input: Text using exactly one colon delimiter and no escaping.
contract.output: A two-item [key, value] collection, or empty when invalid.

examples.explanation: The single colon separates two trimmed fields.

constraints: valid input has exactly two non-empty trimmed fields

blocks.content: The raw input must contain exactly one colon separating a non-empty key and non-empty value. Trim both fields and return them as a two-item collection. Return an empty collection when the colon count or either field is invalid. The current implementation splits on a comma. Correct it.

blocks.title: parse_key_value(text)
blocks.content:
Input: Text using exactly one colon delimiter and no escaping.

Output: A two-item [key, value] collection, or empty when invalid.

blocks.code:
Input
text = " theme : dark "

Output
theme,dark
blocks.caption: The single colon separates two trimmed fields.

blocks.title: Constraints
blocks.content:
0 <= text length <= 1000
delimiter is exactly colon
valid input has exactly two non-empty trimmed fields

blocks.starterCode:
def parse_key_value(text):
    fields = text.split(',')  # Use the declared delimiter and validate fields
    return fields

print(parse_key_value(' theme : dark '))
